summary: SIEM export - per-record retention flags, deletion attestation, and HMAC resume tokens
description:
Issue summary: FinSight needs an on-demand SIEM export that includes (1) a per-event retention flag indicating whether an event is eligible for customer-initiated deletion, (2) a cryptographically signed attestation that a requested deletion window was applied to the exported slice, and (3) HMACed resume tokens so their downstream receiver can perform gap-resilient ingest.

Impact: Customer cannot complete legal hold verification with their internal compliance team without both the per-record retention metadata and a verifiable deletion attestation. This is blocking their SOC2 evidence package for Q2 readiness.

Environment: Redwood production, tenant=fin_sight_prod, region=us-east-1, SIEM bridge configured to push to customer's S3/Hec endpoint.

Steps to reproduce / request details:
1) Customer requests an on-demand export for tenant fin_sight_prod for time window 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z -> 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z.
2) Export must include a field audit.retention_flag with values {retain, deletable, pending-review}.
3) Export bundle must contain a signed deletion_attestation.json manifest (RFC3161-style timestamp + SHA256 manifest of deleted record ids / hashed identifiers).
4) Each CompressedDelta file should include a resume_token header HMACed with customer's shared secret.
5) Customer requests a sample package (first 1M events) and a full runback plan for weekly incremental exports thereafter.

Expected behavior: Redwood produces an export package with the described fields, a signed manifest proving which records were removed due to a tenant-scoped deletion request, and HMACed tokens so the customer's SIEM can verify continuity.

Actual / current behavior: Customer has successfully received standard SIEM deltas but they lack per-record retention metadata and there is no signed deletion attestation format currently available in our default export. They also requested HMACed resume tokens which are not in the standard header today.

Attachments: sample_export_request.json (attached by customer), screenshot of customer's compliance checklist, link to customer's ingestion spec (provided below).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Opened ticket with FinSight's SOC team request and attached sample_export_request.json. Escalating to infra for feasibility and legal for attestation format.

2026-03-11 - Marco Nguyen: Initial triage complete. Serving-runtime team: per-event metadata already exists in our internal audit schema (event.metadata.retention_state) but not exported for SIEM. Need to confirm safe exposure and PII considerations. Engineering to evaluate adding retention_flag mapping to export pipeline. Linked INT-991 for schema change.

2026-03-12 - Legal (Sara Donovan): Suggested attestation should include: (a) RFC3161-compatible timestamp, (b) canonical list of hashed identifiers (SHA256 with tenant salt) for records removed, (c) signature using our HSM key. Asked for retention policy doc from customer to verify mapping to 'pending-review'.

2026-03-13 - Marco Nguyen: Engineering note: two implementation options - a) generate deletion_attestation.json as part of export job using existing audit ledger checkpoints and sign with HSM (preferred), b) provide a verification endpoint that returns on-request signed attestations (requires access controls). Option (a) estimated 4 engineer-days to implement and 1 day QA. Also proposing inclusion of resume_token HMAC header: X-Resume-Token-HMAC. Need secrets exchange with customer for HMAC key or use per-tenant derived secret from their KMS binding.

2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel (Customer): Customer replied with retention policy doc and asked for sample manifest format and a timeline for the sample 1M event package. They also asked whether the attestation will be verifiable by their internal auditors (they prefer ed25519 signatures).
investigation_notes:
Findings: internal audit pipeline contains event.metadata.retention_state and event.id (uuid). We currently compute ledger checkpoints with SHA256 of raw event bytes, but we don't produce a canonical hashed list of removed IDs. HSM team confirmed we can sign arbitrary blobs with tenant-signing-key alias 'signing/exports' with owner approval. Engineering risks: exposing retention_state might reveal sensitive teardown signals; must map internal states to customer-friendly flags and redact any PII fields.

Hypothesis: We can satisfy request by (1) adding a per-export transformer that emits audit.retention_flag and canonical_identifier (sha256(event.id + tenant_salt)), (2) include deletion_attestation.json containing RFC3161 timestamp, canonical list hash, and HSM signature, (3) add X-Resume-Token-HMAC header to delta objects.

Work items created: INT-991 (schema-and-transform), INT-1002 (hsm-signing-workflow), INT-1003 (siem-bridge-header-and-s3-manifest).
resolution:
Workaround supplied: On 2026-03-13 we provided a manually-generated sample package (1,000 events) that includes event.retention_flag and a provisional deletion_attestation signed with a staging key. Customer validated format.

Next steps / targeted fix: Engineering will implement automated deletion_attestation generation and HMACed resume tokens. ETA for production-ready export and HSM-signed manifest: 2026-03-22 (subject to keys approval). Please confirm whether customer requires ed25519 or can accept RSA-PSS signing; legal prefers ed25519 if feasible.

Open follow-ups: obtain customer's HMAC key exchange method (KMS-wrapped or shared secret), confirm acceptable signature algorithm, and schedule a validation run for a 1M event slice in a non-production sandbox before full export.
